nodes.statement:
A real CPM cell coupled to a real spatio-flux nutrient field through one typed
process (`CpmCellField`) closes the paper's §Cell–environment coupling sense/act loop (Fig 5)
as genuine spatial metabolism: it
runs dynamic-FBA at its own footprint and grows both biologically (biomass) and structurally
(CPM lattice volume). Confirmed: biomass 0.1 -> ~0.37, CPM volume 32 -> 110 px (~3.4x) over
20 ticks, on a 3600-pixel lattice the cell occupies only ~3% of by the end.

nodes.label: The cell measurably depletes the local nutrient it senses before diffusion pa...
nodes.statement:
The cell measurably depletes the local nutrient it senses before diffusion partially
resupplies it — niche construction as a direct spatial-metabolic consequence, not a scripted
trajectory. Confirmed: local footprint glucose concentration peaks at 1.15 (t=2) and falls to
0.94 by t=20, an up-to-~18% local drawdown, while the field-wide glucose total falls by only
~32 of 5940 units — the depletion signature is sharply local to the cell's own footprint and
its immediate diffusive neighborhood, not a field-wide event.

nodes.statement:
The O2-capped dynamic-FBA mechanism forces the optimizer into mixed-acid acetate
overflow (rather than pure aerobic respiration), and that byproduct genuinely diffuses
outward into a spreading plume via spatio-flux's own `DiffusionAdvection` process — the
secretion side of the coupling is as real as the uptake side. Confirmed: field-wide acetate
0 -> ~47.0 over 20 ticks.

nodes.label: Over the same coupling process, a different composite -- a localized glucose ...
nodes.statement: Over the same coupling process, a different composite -- a localized glucose depot, a fast-diffusing acetate byproduct, and an acetate-consuming cell role -- sustains a cell that never touches glucose purely via a spatial metabolic handoff: the consumer's local glucose reads 0.0 the entire run while its biomass still climbs, entirely on diffused acetate. This is the paper's §Cell–cell coupling relational-molecule claim made concrete -- the same acetate is the secretor's metabolic waste and the consumer's sole carbon food, its meaning set by each cell's interface (microbial cross-feeding, morris2013). Confirmed: consumer local_glucose 0.0, local_acetate 1.30, biomass 1.25 -> 3.79, ending as a viable 65-pixel CPM cell.

nodes.statement:
A single real CPM cell coupled to a real spatio-flux acetate field through one
coupling process (`CpmDisintegration`) reproduces the paper's §Disintegration level-shift
(Fig 6) as genuine spatial dissolution: the cell holds coherent while the diffusing acetate
field is below its
footprint-local viability bound, then latches a release once that bound is crossed at a
specific, deterministic tick, and its domain resorbs to full dissolution over the following
ticks. Confirmed: area > 30 through tick 6, released_tick == 7.0, area == 0 by tick 16, all
deterministic across repeated runs.

nodes.label: The cell's shed material does not vanish -- it becomes physical debris. As th...
nodes.statement:
The cell's shed material does not vanish -- it becomes physical debris. As the
domain resorbs, its vacated footprint pixels are converted into particles in a shared
map[particle] store, and that debris cloud keeps scattering (RMS spread strictly increasing)
well after the cell itself has fully dissolved, under a separate stock BrownianMovement
process. Confirmed: 68 particles shed by tick 16, RMS spread ~5.3 -> ~7.6 over an 8-tick
post-dissolution window.

nodes.statement: A Cahn-Hilliard composition field realizes the condensate mechanism the paper draws from banani2017 (§Molecular compositions, Fig 8): weak-interaction-driven phase separation into droplets with an emergent interface. Confirmed as spinodal decomposition: a near-critical field separates into two phases (variance ~7e-5 -> ~0.38 over 10000 steps) bounded by a sharp interface, with total mass conserved to ~4e-18 and the field bounded in [-1, 1]. A boundary forms out of a well-mixed medium, mass-conserved.

nodes.label: Honesty point, load-bearing for the paper's central question. The condensate ...
nodes.statement: Honesty point, load-bearing for the paper's central question. The condensate study demonstrates a boundary forming -- phase separation, mass-conserved, with an emergent interface -- but NOT the condensate doing interface work: it does not selectively concentrate or exclude a second species. That selective-permeability property is exactly what would make the interface a functional, regulatable boundary rather than a transient or unregulated aggregate, which is the discriminator the paper's §Molecular compositions question (Fig 8) turns on. It is named here as the natural next step, not claimed as already shown. Likewise the sorting study demonstrates differential-adhesion demixing with a cohesion guard, not a molecular binding-affinity/selectivity term.

nodes.statement: The demixing is caused by the differential-J regime, not by CPM dynamics per se. Under neutral contact energies (all J=8) the same checkerboard at T=10 stays mixed, isolating the complementarity-encoding contact-energy asymmetry as the cause of sorting. Confirmed by a neutral-J composite re-run (documented, not a committed test): neutral J holds hetero_frac ~0.52 over 600 MCS vs ~0.06 for the differential-J regime.
